significance: One of the eight Atta-veerattanam shrines of Shiva, built in the 9th century under the Cholas and enlarged by the Thanjavur Nayaks; it holds an 11th-century bronze of Shiva as slayer of the elephant demon.
story: Challenged by sages who doubted his power, Shiva is said to have taken the Gajasamhara form here, killing the elephant demon and wearing its hide as a garment.
